line: I'm making a snack. Want one?
followUps: Sweet or salty?
Want to eat it in here or take it with you?
shareBack: Mention one small thing from your day while you cook, then leave space.
deliveryCue: Say it in passing and carry on; let them come to you.

line: You pick the music. I want to hear what you're into right now.
followUps: What do you like about this one?
Who introduced you to them?
shareBack: Mention one song you loved at their age, briefly, then let the music play.
deliveryCue: Eyes on the road, and no comments on their taste.

line: Saw this and thought of you. No need to reply.
followUps: What's the funniest thing you've seen this week?
Got one to send back?
shareBack: If they answer, reply with one line or an emoji, not a question about school or work.
deliveryCue: Send it with the picture or clip and leave it there.

line: Proud of you for today. That's all.
followUps: What part are you happiest with?
What do you want to do to celebrate?
shareBack: Later, mention the exact thing you noticed them do, then let them take it from there.
deliveryCue: Send it and leave it; no question straight after.

line: Getting food on my way home. Want anything?
followUps: Same as last time?
Anything for later as well?
shareBack: Say what you're getting for yourself, then eat together if they're up for it.
deliveryCue: A yes or no is a full answer; don't push for more.

line: Good luck today. I'm around later if you want to tell me about it.
followUps: Which part went best?
What do you need tonight?
shareBack: If they bring it up, mention a time you were nervous before something, in a sentence.
deliveryCue: Wait for them to raise it later; don't open with a question.

line: Sorry I was short this morning. That was about me, not you.
followUps: Is there anything you wanted to say that I cut off?
Can we start over tonight?
shareBack: Tonight, say in one sentence what was going on for you, then let them respond or not.
deliveryCue: Don't add 'but'. Send it and let it land.

line: Drive-through run tonight? My treat.
followUps: Where do you want to go?
Want to bring anyone?
shareBack: In the car, mention one small thing from your day, then let them pick the music.
deliveryCue: Keep it an offer; no agenda once you're in the car.

line: I had a weird day. Want to hear the dumbest part?
followUps: Has anything like that happened to you?
What would you have done?
shareBack: Keep your story under a minute, then leave room for one of theirs.
deliveryCue: Side by side works best: cooking, driving, tidying up.

line: I need your opinion on something. Which of these would you pick?
followUps: What makes that one better?
What would you change about it?
shareBack: Say which one you were leaning toward, then go with theirs if you can.
deliveryCue: Ask about something real, and take the answer seriously.

line: If you want a break from the table, I could use a hand in the kitchen.
followUps: Who have you ended up stuck next to?
Want to be in charge of dessert?
shareBack: Mention who you find hard work at these things, quietly, then share the job.
deliveryCue: Say it quietly, as a way out, not a chore.

line: What are you watching lately that I'd actually like?
followUps: What's it about, without spoilers?
Can we watch the first one together?
shareBack: Mention one show you're in the middle of, then let them choose what goes on.
deliveryCue: One question, then stop. Follow up only if they light up.

line: You don't have to talk to everyone today. Give me a look if you need rescuing.
followUps: Who are you actually glad to see?
What would make today easier?
shareBack: Mention who you'd like rescuing from, then agree on a signal.
deliveryCue: Say it on the way there or early on, just the two of you.

line: You seem worn out this week. I'm not going to quiz you. I'm here if you want to talk.
followUps: Do you want ideas, or just someone to listen?
What would make this week easier?
shareBack: If they open up, mention one time you felt the same, in a sentence, then go back to them.
deliveryCue: Only if you've noticed it. Say it once, then leave a long pause.

line: Can you show me how this works? I keep getting it wrong.
followUps: How did you work that out?
What else can it do?
shareBack: Mention what you were trying to do with it, then let them drive.
deliveryCue: Hand over the phone or controller and let them be the expert.

line: Someone needs to pick the movie for after dinner. I vote you.
followUps: What are the options?
What should we definitely not watch?
shareBack: Offer one movie you'd veto, then back their choice in front of everyone.
deliveryCue: Say it with a grin, where they can say no easily.

line: When I was your age I worried a lot about fitting in. I don't know if it's like that for you.
followUps: What's it like with your friends right now?
What do you wish adults understood about it?
shareBack: Offer one short, true story from that age, then let them decide whether to add theirs.
deliveryCue: Say it and stop. Let the silence do the work.

line: What was the funniest thing that happened today?
followUps: What happened next?
Who else was laughing?
shareBack: Tell them one funny thing from your own day, then ask if anything else made them laugh.
deliveryCue: Try at bedtime or one-on-one, not the moment you see them.

line: Who did you sit with at lunch today?
followUps: What did you two talk about?
What did you have to eat?
shareBack: Mention who you had lunch with, then ask who they'd like to sit with tomorrow.
deliveryCue: Ask after a snack, once they've had a few quiet minutes.

line: What was the hardest part of today?
followUps: What did you do when that happened?
What would help next time?
shareBack: Mention one small hard thing from your day and what you did, then give them a hug.
deliveryCue: Bedtime, lights low. Listen; don't fix it.

line: What was your favorite part of practice today?
followUps: What made that part fun?
What do you want to try next time?
shareBack: Mention the part you most enjoyed watching, then ask what they'd like for a snack.
deliveryCue: Ask on the walk to the car, not in front of the others.

line: I loved watching you keep trying out there. Which part felt best?
followUps: What were you thinking when you did that?
What do you want to show me next time?
shareBack: Mention the exact moment you noticed, then let them tell you about it.
deliveryCue: Praise the effort, not the score. Say it right after.

line: I'm so glad I got to watch you today.
followUps: What was the most fun part?
Who were you playing with?
shareBack: Mention one thing you liked seeing, then let them choose what to talk about.
deliveryCue: Say it and stop; no coaching on the way home.

line: Who made you laugh today?
followUps: What did they do?
What did you do then?
shareBack: Tell them who made you laugh today, then ask who they want to play with tomorrow.
deliveryCue: Good in the car or while you're doing something side by side.

line: What's your favorite thing on the table?
followUps: What does it taste like?
What should we try next?
shareBack: Point out your own favorite, then ask which one they'd like to help make next year.
deliveryCue: Ask quietly, beside them, not across the table.

line: Who do you want to play with after we eat?
followUps: What game will you play?
Can anyone join in?
shareBack: Mention who you're looking forward to talking to, then ask what they need for the game.
deliveryCue: Ask before the meal, down at their level.

line: What are you most excited about today?
followUps: What do you think it will be like?
What do you want to do first?
shareBack: Tell them the one thing you're excited about, then ask how you can help with theirs.
deliveryCue: Ask at breakfast or in the car on the way.

line: I need a helper. Do you want to stir or set the table?
followUps: How should we do it?
What should we do next?
shareBack: Tell them what you used to help with at their age, then ask what job they'd like next.
deliveryCue: Give two choices and let them pick; chat while you work.

line: Show me what you made today. I want to hear how you did it.
followUps: Which part took the longest?
What will you make next?
shareBack: Point to the one detail you like best, then ask where it should go.
deliveryCue: Get down to their level and look properly before you speak.

line: I can't decide what to read tonight. Which book should we pick?
followUps: What do you like about that one?
Which part should I do the voices for?
shareBack: Mention a book you loved when you were small, then start reading theirs.
deliveryCue: Ask at bedtime, once teeth are done.

line: You were so patient at the table. What was the best part of dinner?
followUps: Who did you like talking to?
What should we have next time?
shareBack: Tell them your best part, then ask what they want to do now.
deliveryCue: Say it afterwards, just the two of you.

line: Tell me one good thing and one not-so-good thing from today.
followUps: What happened with the not-so-good one?
Which one do you want to talk about first?
shareBack: Give your own good thing and not-so-good thing, kept small, then ask which of theirs to hear more about.
deliveryCue: Good at bedtime or bath time, when there's no rush.

line: Was today more sunny or more stormy?
followUps: What made it sunny?
Was there a cloudy bit in there?
shareBack: Say what your own day's weather was and one reason, then ask what tomorrow's forecast looks like.
deliveryCue: Take whatever weather they pick without arguing with it.

line: You seemed quiet after school. I'm here if something's on your mind.
followUps: Do you want to tell me about it, or have a hug first?
Is it a big thing or a small thing?
shareBack: Mention a time you felt quiet as a kid, in one sentence, then let them lead.
deliveryCue: Only if you've noticed it. Sit beside them and wait; silence is fine.

line: Who was kind to you today?
followUps: What did they do?
Did you get to be kind to anyone back?
shareBack: Tell them who was kind to you today and what they did, then ask who they might be kind to tomorrow.
deliveryCue: Ask in the car or at bedtime, when it's just the two of you.

line: Was anything today a little bit scary or tricky?
followUps: What helped, even a little?
Is it still on your mind?
shareBack: Mention something small that felt tricky for you today and what you did, then ask if they want a hug.
deliveryCue: Bedtime, lights low. Listen and name the feeling; skip the "why."

line: If you could change one rule in our house, which one would it be?
followUps: What would the new rule be?
Which rule should we definitely keep?
shareBack: Name a rule you'd change too, then talk about whether you could try one of theirs.
deliveryCue: Take the answer seriously, even a silly one.

line: What's something you're really good at that grown-ups don't notice?
followUps: How did you get so good at it?
Can you show me sometime?
shareBack: Mention something you were good at as a kid that nobody saw, then ask for a demonstration.
deliveryCue: One-on-one, when you have time to watch whatever they show you.

line: What do you think makes someone a good friend?
followUps: Who's been a good friend to you?
What do you do to be a good friend?
shareBack: Mention one thing a good friend once did for you, then ask what they would add.
deliveryCue: At bedtime or on a walk. A short answer is fine.

line: What's something that used to scare you that isn't scary anymore?
followUps: What changed?
Is anything a little scary right now?
shareBack: Share one thing that scared you as a kid and how it stopped, then ask what they would tell a younger kid.
deliveryCue: Keep it light at bedtime; let them decide how far to go.

line: I love spending time with you. What do you like best that we do together?
followUps: What makes that one the best?
What's something we've never done together that you'd like to?
shareBack: Name your own favorite thing you do together, then pick when to do it next.
deliveryCue: At bedtime, or at the end of a good day together.

line: Looks like today was a hard one. Do you want a hug, or some quiet time with me nearby?
followUps: Do you want to tell me about it now or later?
What would help right now?
shareBack: If they talk, mention a time you had a hard day too, in a sentence, then stay close.
deliveryCue: Then stay close. No fixing, and no more questions for a while.

line: That sounds like it felt really big. I'm right here.
followUps: Do you want to tell me more, or just sit for a bit?
What would help a little right now?
shareBack: If they ask, say you've had big feelings too and they passed, then stay with them.
deliveryCue: Name the feeling if you can; skip the "why."

line: Want to read something together, just you and me?
followUps: Which one should we pick?
Want to snuggle up here or on your bed?
shareBack: Mention a book that made you feel better as a kid, then start reading theirs.
deliveryCue: A good offer after a hard day. Let the story do the comforting.

line: It's okay to be sad about it. I'd be sad too.
followUps: What part feels the saddest?
Do you want to do something cozy together?
shareBack: Mention one time you felt sad about something like it, briefly, then let them talk or not.
deliveryCue: Say it calmly and stay nearby. Don't rush to cheer them up.

line: Let's take a walk around the block, just the two of us.
followUps: What should we look for on the way?
Is anything on your mind today?
shareBack: Point out one thing you notice on the walk, then let them set the pace and the topic.
deliveryCue: Side by side and moving is easier than face to face after a hard day.

line: I'm sorry I yelled earlier. That wasn't fair to you.
followUps: Is there anything you wanted to say back then?
Can we have a do-over?
shareBack: Say in one sentence what you'll try next time you're upset, then offer a hug if they want one.
deliveryCue: Get down to their level. Don't add "but you…"

line: I made a mistake today, and I want to make it right. Can we start again?
followUps: What would help make it better?
What should we do first in our do-over?
shareBack: Name the mistake simply, in kid words, then let them choose the do-over.
deliveryCue: Keep it short and calm, once everyone has settled down.

line: We both got pretty upset. I love you even when we're mad at each other.
followUps: Are you still feeling mad?
What could help us next time?
shareBack: Say one thing you'll do differently, then ask what they could try too.
deliveryCue: Wait until you are both calm, then sit close.

line: I broke my promise about the park. I'm sorry. Let's pick a day that works.
followUps: Which day should we go?
What should we do first when we get there?
shareBack: Say what got in the way, in a sentence, then put the new day somewhere they can see it.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real promise, and only offer a day you can keep.

line: Want to draw something together? I'll start with a silly one.
followUps: What should I add to it?
What are you drawing?
shareBack: Draw something about the two of you, then let them add to it.
deliveryCue: A gentle way back in after a fight, once you've said sorry.

line: Saturday morning is just for us. Pancakes or the playground first?
followUps: What should we do after that?
Who gets to pick next time?
shareBack: Say which one you're hoping for, then go with their pick.
deliveryCue: Offer two choices you can really do, and let them pick.

line: Let's build something this weekend. A fort, a cardboard car, or a rocket?
followUps: What will we need?
Where should we build it?
shareBack: Mention something you built as a kid, then start a list of supplies together.
deliveryCue: Ask early in the week so they have something to look forward to.

line: If we had a whole day off together, what would we do?
followUps: What would we eat?
Which part could we really do soon?
shareBack: Add one thing from your own dream day, then pick one piece to do this month.
deliveryCue: Good in the car. Then actually do one small part of it.

line: I want to learn a new game. Will you teach me one this week?
followUps: What are the rules?
When should we play?
shareBack: Mention a game you loved at their age, then offer to teach it after theirs.
deliveryCue: Let them be in charge of the rules, even if the rules change.

line: You did it! Tell me the whole story, from the start.
followUps: What was the hardest part?
How did it feel when you finished?
shareBack: Say the exact moment you were proudest of, then ask how they want to celebrate.
deliveryCue: Say it right away, with real excitement, and let them talk.

line: You worked so hard at that. How do you want to celebrate?
followUps: What part are you proudest of?
Who do you want to tell?
shareBack: Mention one thing you noticed them practice, then pick a small celebration together.
deliveryCue: Praise the effort, not just the result.

line: That was a big first! What part do you want to remember most?
followUps: What were you thinking right before?
What do you want to try next?
shareBack: Tell them about one of your own firsts at their age, briefly, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: For firsts: a lost tooth, a bike ride, a sleepover, a swim.

line: No big talk needed. Just checking that this week is going okay for you.
followUps: Anything this week you're dreading or looking forward to?
Anything I can take off your plate?
shareBack: Mention one thing about your own week, in a line, then leave it with them.
deliveryCue: Text it or say it in passing. A thumbs-up counts as an answer.

line: This week looks like a lot. On a scale from fine to drowning, where are you?
followUps: What's the biggest thing on the list?
Want help with any of it, or just a heads-up?
shareBack: Give your own number for the week and one reason, then ask if there is anything you can do.
deliveryCue: Keep it light. Whatever number they give, don't lecture.

line: You've been quieter lately. Not prying, just noticing. I'm around.
followUps: Is it something going on, or just a lot of everything?
Want company or space?
shareBack: If they open up, mention a time you went quiet at their age, in a sentence, then go back to them.
deliveryCue: Only if you've noticed it. Say it once, then drop it.

line: Thinking about you today. Hope the big thing goes well. No need to reply.
followUps: How did it end up going?
Want to do something to unwind tonight?
shareBack: If they reply, answer with one line about your own day, not another question.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real event. Send it before, not during.

line: Send me your day in one emoji. Mine's a coffee cup.
followUps: What's the story behind that one?
Better or worse than yesterday?
shareBack: Explain your own emoji in one line, then let the thread rest.
deliveryCue: Any emoji back is a win; don't push for more.

line: I keep wondering what I'd tell myself at your age. What would you tell a kid a few years younger?
followUps: What do you wish someone had told you?
What have you figured out that adults haven't?
shareBack: Offer one thing you'd tell your younger self, in a sentence, then let them add or not.
deliveryCue: Best side by side: a drive, a walk, the dishes.

line: I read something today that got me thinking, and I'd like your take on it.
followUps: What do you think most people your age would say?
Has your view on it changed over time?
shareBack: Give your own view in a sentence or two, and say so if theirs changes your mind.
deliveryCue: Pick a real topic, not a lesson in disguise. Send the link if texting.

line: You handled that situation with your friend really well. I don't think I could have at your age.
followUps: How did you figure out what to do?
Was it harder than it looked?
shareBack: Mention one time you handled something like it badly, briefly, then let them talk.
deliveryCue: Only if it is true. Swap in what you actually saw.

line: What's something you believe now that you didn't a year ago?
followUps: What changed your mind?
Do your friends see it the same way?
shareBack: Name one thing you've changed your mind about recently, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: Ask once, in the car or by text, and accept "I don't know."

line: I don't say it enough: I like who you're becoming.
followUps: What do you want to get better at?
What are you proudest of lately?
shareBack: Name one specific thing you saw them do lately that made you think it.
deliveryCue: Say it and stop. Let them respond when they are ready.

line: Is there anything you wish I understood better about your life right now?
followUps: What would help me get it?
Is there something I do that makes it harder?
shareBack: Thank them, say one thing you'll try, and don't defend yourself.
deliveryCue: Only ask if you are ready to hear the answer without arguing.

line: Looks like it was a rough day. I'm around if you want company.
followUps: Want to talk about it, or do something to take your mind off it?
Anything I can do tonight?
shareBack: If they talk, mention a rough day you had at their age, in one sentence, then go back to listening.
deliveryCue: Say it once, then leave it. Being nearby is enough.

line: You don't have to tell me about it. If you ever want to, I'll just listen.
followUps: Do you want my opinion, or just an ear?
Is there anything that would make tonight easier?
shareBack: Hold your own story unless they ask; if they do, keep it to a sentence.
deliveryCue: Then really just listen. No advice unless they ask.

line: No need to reply. I love you and I'm on your side.
followUps: Want me to pick you up?
Anything you need from me tonight?
shareBack: If they reply, answer with one warm line, not a question about what happened.
deliveryCue: Send it and leave it. Don't follow up with another text.

line: Want to go for a drive? You pick the music, and we don't have to talk.
followUps: Anywhere you want to go?
Want to grab food on the way?
shareBack: Stay quiet unless they start talking; if they do, listen more than you speak.
deliveryCue: Car rides help because nobody has to look at anyone.

line: That sounds awful. I'm sorry it happened.
followUps: Do you want help with it, or do you just need to vent?
What would make tomorrow easier?
shareBack: Only if they want it, mention a time something similar happened to you, briefly.
deliveryCue: Say it before anything else. No "at least" and no lesson.

line: I overreacted earlier, and I'm sorry. You didn't deserve that.
followUps: Is there anything you want to say about it?
Can we try that conversation again?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what was going on with you, without turning it into a "but."
deliveryCue: Don't add "but." Say it once and let them respond, or not.

line: I've been thinking about our argument. I was wrong about part of it, and I want to hear your side properly.
followUps: What did I miss?
What would feel fair to you?
shareBack: Name the part you got wrong plainly, then listen to the rest without defending.
deliveryCue: Wait a few hours. A text is fine if face to face feels like too much.

line: I don't want this fight hanging over us. Can we reset?
followUps: Is anything still bugging you about it?
What should we do differently next time?
shareBack: Say one thing you'll do differently, then ask if they'll meet you halfway.
deliveryCue: Keep it short. Offer a snack or a drive to go with it.

line: I came down hard on you about that. The rule stands, and I should have said it more kindly.
followUps: How did it come across to you?
Is there a version of the rule you think is fairer?
shareBack: Explain in a sentence what worried you, then really consider their idea.
deliveryCue: For when you still mean the rule but regret the tone.

line: Peace offering: I'm getting your favorite on the way home.
followUps: Want to talk later, or just eat?
Anything else you want?
shareBack: When you are together, say sorry in a sentence and let the food do the rest.
deliveryCue: Pair it with a real apology in person; the food doesn't replace it.

line: I'd like a day with just the two of us. You pick, I'll pay.
followUps: What sounds good?
Which weekend works for you?
shareBack: Mention one thing you'd enjoy too, then go with their pick.
deliveryCue: Mean the "you pick" part, even if it isn't your thing.

line: Want to learn something new together this month? Climbing, cooking, anything.
followUps: What have you always wanted to try?
Want to bring a friend?
shareBack: Name one thing you've always wanted to try, then let them choose.
deliveryCue: Give two or three real options and an easy no.

line: That movie you mentioned comes out Friday. Want to go?
followUps: Want to get food before or after?
Want to bring someone?
shareBack: Mention what you're looking forward to about it, then sort the tickets.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real thing they mentioned. A no is fine.

line: Breakfast out on Saturday, just us? Totally fine if you would rather sleep in.
followUps: Where should we go?
Early or late?
shareBack: Mention a place you used to go at their age, then let them pick.
deliveryCue: Keep the out real; don't sulk if they pass.

line: Can you help me plan our next trip? You get a real vote.
followUps: Where would you go if it were up to you?
What would make it fun for you?
shareBack: Share one place you'd love to go, then take their ideas seriously.
deliveryCue: Only ask if their vote will actually count.

line: Heard the news. That's huge! Tell me everything when you're home.
followUps: What was it like when you found out?
Who else have you told?
shareBack: Tell them what you felt when you heard, in a sentence, then let them do the talking.
deliveryCue: Text it right away; save the questions for in person.

line: I saw how hard you worked for that. Congratulations.
followUps: What part are you proudest of?
How do you want to celebrate?
shareBack: Mention the exact moment you noticed their effort, then ask what comes next for them.
deliveryCue: Praise the effort they put in, not just the result.

line: Your pick for dinner tonight. You earned it.
followUps: What do you want?
Want anyone else to come?
shareBack: Over dinner, say one specific thing you're proud of, then let them tell the story.
deliveryCue: Say it after good news, and let them choose without comment.

line: Okay, I need the full story of how it happened.
followUps: When did you know it was going to work out?
What was the hardest part getting there?
shareBack: React to the best part with real enthusiasm, then ask what they want to do next.
deliveryCue: Use it right after big news. Then mostly listen.

line: That was a big deal, and you made it look easy.
followUps: Was it as easy as it looked?
What's next?
shareBack: Mention the part you'd have found hard at their age, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: Swap in what they actually did, and only if it fits.

line: Been thinking about you. What's been the best part of your week so far?
followUps: What made it good?
Anything coming up you're looking forward to?
shareBack: Share the best part of your own week in a line, then ask what is next for them.
deliveryCue: Good by text midweek. Skip questions about grades or work.

line: Is the new place starting to feel like home yet?
followUps: What's the best thing about it?
Anything you still need for it?
shareBack: Mention what your first place on your own was like, in a line, then ask if they want anything sent.
deliveryCue: Swap in what is new: a dorm, an apartment, a city.

line: Sounds like you have a lot on. Is it the good kind of busy, or the other kind?
followUps: What's taking the most out of you?
Anything I can do from here?
shareBack: Mention a time you were overloaded at their stage, in a sentence, then go back to them.
deliveryCue: Ask once. Take "fine" at face value and leave the door open.

line: I'm not checking up on you, I promise. I just like knowing what your days look like now.
followUps: What does a normal weekday look like?
What's the part you like most?
shareBack: Describe a normal day of yours in a line or two, then ask what they'd change about theirs.
deliveryCue: Mean the "not checking up" part. No follow-up on chores or grades.

line: You sounded tired last time we talked. Anything weighing on you, or just a long week?
followUps: Do you want ideas, or just to vent?
What would make this week a bit easier?
shareBack: Mention a time you felt that way at their stage, briefly, then let them lead.
deliveryCue: Only if you noticed it. Accept "just a long week."

line: What's been the hardest part of being on your own so far?
followUps: What's turned out easier than you expected?
What do you wish you had known before?
shareBack: Share the hardest part of your own first year away, in a sentence, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: Ask when there is time for a real answer, not in between other things.

line: Settle a debate for me: what's the most overrated food?
followUps: What should everyone eat instead?
Has anyone ever agreed with you on that?
shareBack: Give your own overrated pick, argue for it badly, then concede.
deliveryCue: Send it out of the blue. It works because nothing rides on it.

line: Found an old photo of you at the beach. Do you remember that trip?
followUps: What do you remember most about it?
Should we go back sometime?
shareBack: Mention the moment you remember from that trip, then send the photo.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real photo and send it with the text.

line: What are you cooking these days? I need new ideas.
followUps: Where did you learn that one?
Can you send me the recipe?
shareBack: Mention what you have been cooking on repeat, then offer a recipe swap.
deliveryCue: Ask for real, and actually try what they suggest.

line: I need something new to listen to on my commute. What would you pick for me?
followUps: What do you like about it?
What else are you into lately?
shareBack: Report back after you listen, with one honest thought.
deliveryCue: Then actually listen to it, and tell them what you thought.

line: What's something you've gotten into lately that I probably don't know about?
followUps: How did you get into it?
Can you show me sometime?
shareBack: Mention one new thing you have gotten into, then ask for their recommendation.
deliveryCue: Be curious, not skeptical, whatever it turns out to be.

line: Now that you're grown, I'd love to hear how you remember growing up. What stands out?
followUps: What do you think we got right?
What would you do differently, if it were you?
shareBack: Share one memory of theirs you treasure, then ask what they would like to hear from your side.
deliveryCue: Ask when there's time, and don't defend yourself if something stings.

line: I'd love to know what you're figuring out these days, not just what you're doing.
followUps: What's surprised you about yourself lately?
What are you still undecided about?
shareBack: Share one thing you are still figuring out at your age, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: Better on a long call or a walk than in a quick text.

line: Is there anything you wish I had told you before you moved out?
followUps: What did you have to learn the hard way?
What should I tell someone younger?
shareBack: Share one thing you learned the hard way at their age, then ask what they would add.
deliveryCue: Take whatever they say as useful, not as criticism.

line: I'm weighing a big decision, and I'd value your take, adult to adult.
followUps: What would you do in my shoes?
What am I not seeing?
shareBack: Explain what's pulling you each way in a sentence or two, then really consider their view.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real decision, and only ask if you will weigh the answer.

line: I've never really told you how unsure I felt when you were little. I was figuring it out as I went.
followUps: Did it ever show?
What do you remember from those years?
shareBack: Tell one short story from those years, then ask what they are figuring out as they go now.
deliveryCue: In person or on a call, when there is time. Not by text.

line: What's mattering more to you these days than it used to?
followUps: What changed it?
What's mattering less?
shareBack: Name one thing that matters more to you now than it did at their age, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: Good on a long drive or a late call.

line: No agenda, just want to hear your voice. Got ten minutes this week?
followUps: What's been taking up most of your time?
When's a good time?
shareBack: On the call, share one small thing from home, then let them steer.
deliveryCue: Let them pick the time, and keep it short if they are busy.

line: It's been too long since we caught up properly. Free for a call this weekend?
followUps: What's the best time?
Anything you want to tell me about first?
shareBack: On the call, share one thing from home that made you think of them, then let them steer.
deliveryCue: Short and easy to say yes to. Suggest a time.

line: Your team won last night. Thought of you.
followUps: Did you watch it?
Who are they playing next?
shareBack: Mention one moment from the game you liked, then let the thread go where it goes.
deliveryCue: Swap in something you know they care about.

line: It's good to have you home. What's the first thing you want to do while you're here?
followUps: Who do you want to see?
Anything you've been craving?
shareBack: Mention one thing you have been saving to do with them, then let them plan around it.
deliveryCue: Say it soon after they arrive, before the schedule fills up.

line: Drove past your old favorite spot today. Still open. Made me think of you.
followUps: Do you still think about going there?
Should we go next time you are home?
shareBack: Mention a memory from that place, in a line, then suggest going together.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real place: a diner, a park, a shop.

line: Thinking of you today, and I'm on your side. No need to reply.
followUps: Want to talk tonight, or would a distraction be better?
Is there anything I can send you?
shareBack: If they reply, answer with one warm line. Save your own news for another day.
deliveryCue: Send it and leave it. One text is enough.

line: Would a call help, or would you rather I just keep sending you silly things?
followUps: What time works for a call?
Want the silly things anyway?
shareBack: Do whichever they pick, and keep your own updates short for now.
deliveryCue: Either answer is a real answer. Follow their lead.

line: That sounds really hard. I'm sorry you're going through it, and I'm glad you told me.
followUps: Do you want ideas, or would it help more to just talk it out?
What would make this week a little easier?
shareBack: If it helps, mention a time you went through something similar, in a sentence, then go back to them.
deliveryCue: No "at least," and no advice unless they ask.

line: I can send a care package this week. What would actually help?
followUps: Food, or something for your place?
Anything you've been running low on?
shareBack: Mention one thing you are putting in already, then add whatever they ask for.
deliveryCue: Send something even if they say "nothing."

line: I can come up for a weekend if that would help. No pressure either way.
followUps: Which weekend would be best?
Would you rather I just call more often?
shareBack: Say what you'd like to do while you're there, briefly, then let them set the plan.
deliveryCue: Only offer it if you can really go.

line: You don't have to have it all figured out. I'm proud of you anyway.
followUps: What's weighing on you most?
What would feel like a small win this week?
shareBack: Mention a time you didn't have it figured out at their age, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: After a setback: a rejection, a breakup, a hard semester.

line: When you are home next, can we do breakfast, just the two of us?
followUps: Which morning works best?
Where should we go?
shareBack: Mention a place you'd like to go, then let them choose.
deliveryCue: Leave room for a no; they'll have a lot of people to see.

line: I'd love to come visit and see your life there. When would be a good time?
followUps: What should I make sure to see?
Where should we eat?
shareBack: Mention one thing you'd like to see, then let them plan the visit.
deliveryCue: Let them pick the dates, and keep the first visit short.

line: Want to start a weekly call? Same time each week, and skip it whenever you need to.
followUps: What day works best?
Short and quick, or longer?
shareBack: Suggest a time that suits you, then go with whatever they pick.
deliveryCue: Make skipping easy; that is what keeps it going.

line: Let's do something together while you're back: a hike, a movie, cooking. Your pick.
followUps: What have you been missing about home?
Which day works?
shareBack: Mention which one you'd enjoy most, then go with their choice.
deliveryCue: Keep it to one plan. Their time home goes fast.

line: Congratulations on the new job! What was it like when you found out?
followUps: What are you most excited about?
When do you start?
shareBack: Tell them what you thought when you heard, then ask what they want to do to celebrate.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real news: a job, an exam, a lease, an award.

line: I'm so proud of you. I want to hear how it all came together.
followUps: What was the hardest part?
Who helped you along the way?
shareBack: Mention one thing you saw them do on the way there, then hand the story back.
deliveryCue: Say it right after the news. Save advice for another day.

line: Dinner's on me to celebrate, wherever you want, whenever you're free.
followUps: Where should we go?
Who else do you want there?
shareBack: Make a toast with one specific thing you are proud of, then let them talk.
deliveryCue: Let them pick the place and the people.

line: You finished! That's a lot of hard work behind you. What will you do first?
followUps: What part are you proudest of?
What's next after that?
shareBack: Say what you remember about the day they started, in a line, then ask about what comes next.
deliveryCue: For a graduation, a finished project, or the end of a hard stretch.

line: I was out of line earlier. I'm sorry. Can we start over at dinner?
followUps: Anything you want to say about it?
What should we have tonight?
shareBack: Say once what you will try to do differently, then talk about something else.
deliveryCue: Say it side by side, then drop it. Don't ask for an apology back.

line: I'd like to hear what's been on your mind lately, not just the schedule stuff. No rush.
followUps: What's been taking up the most space?
Is that a good thing or a hard thing right now?
shareBack: Offer one thing that's been on your own mind, in a sentence, then leave room.
deliveryCue: Text it or say it in the car; let a short answer be enough.
